subtasks.title: Compact-card contract for the six metric widgets (data helpers + shared Blade kit)
subtasks.approach: One coherent node because the pieces are mutually dependent: the card data helpers, the `expanded` flag/view swap, and the Blade kit must land together or the widgets point at a view that does not exist. Build the helpers ON TOP of getMonthlyData()/getGraphLabels() in DashboardWidget.php:161-238 without touching their month arithmetic -- that code carries the DEV-1927 fix pinned by tests/Filament/Widgets/Dashboard/DashboardMonthLabelsTest.php, which must keep passing UNMODIFIED. Current-period total costs ZERO new queries: it is already cached under the existing keys ('today'/'last_7d' as in getDescription(), 'this_month' = the last getMonthlyData() bucket, 'last_month' = the 'Y-m' bucket). Only the prior-equivalent-period value is new (one bounded query per metric, per the pct_change decision), and for date='last_month' even that is free because the preceding month's 'Y-m' bucket is already cached. Route the prior-period read through a new `getRangeTotal()` seam that defaults to the existing abstract getModelQueryForDates() (DashboardWidget.php:260) and is OVERRIDDEN in SharedHitStatsData to use getSharedHitStatsForRange() -- mandatory, because the four hit widgets stub getModelQueryForDates() to `return 0` (LiveHits.php:31-34) and their real data comes from the single batched HitStatsBatchQuery (FINAL, bounded, org-scoped). This keeps the 4-hits-in-one-query property and all FINAL / _peerdb_is_deleted hygiene, since no new SQL is written at all. Covers the six 'buggy' metric-widget sites: ScanCount, LiveHits, StagingLiveHits and StagingHistoricalHits should need NO per-file edit (the card path is inherited); RecoveryCounts and HistoricalHits are relabelled in t3.

subtasks.title: Dashboard page: single expanded-card key, 2x4 grid, one shared detail region
subtasks.approach: Implements the binding architecture (Q8 option b): the expanded key is a scalar property on the PAGE, so 'only one open, opening a new one replaces the old' is structural rather than enforced by logic, and the expensive chart widget is not mounted at all until a card is clicked (Filament widgets are lazy, and DashboardWidget::mount() deliberately skips ChartWidget::mount()'s data checksum, so the collapsed grid runs no chart queries). Restructure the widget registration: today the eight cards would arrive via getFooterWidgets() (Dashboard.php:69-83), which the page layout renders AFTER content() -- that would place the shared detail region above the grid. Move the cards into getWidgets() and compose content() = filters form, card grid, detail region, so the region sits BELOW the whole grid as decided. Also drops KitStatusGraph from the registration list (t7 deletes the class afterwards, so the page is never registered-but-missing). Do NOT touch filtersForm()/updatedFilters() or the 'refresh-dashboard' dispatch at line 107 -- that event is shared with ClientAnalytics.php:166, IndividualClientAnalytics.php:55,191 and Client/ClientTable.php:46, and it is also what already makes the cards follow the page date filter (DashboardWidget::refreshData). Do not touch canAccess()/mount(): access control is out of scope, which is why this node carries no auth blast-radius tag.

subtasks.title: Kit Users card (Camera Kits + Kit Users) and remove the Active/Inactive filter
subtasks.approach: Per Q5, do not redefine Kit Users: Camera Kits = total org kit count, Kit Users = the ACTIVE kit-user count the donut already computed. Take the active number from the EXISTING cachedActiveKitIds() list (KitUsers.php:35-54) rather than porting KitStatusGraph::active() -- same population (DISTINCT kit_id over the same 3-day ClickHouse scan window), one fewer ClickHouse round trip, and it guarantees the headline number always equals the number of rows in the expanded list. No cross-connection query at all, so the Kit(zod)/KitSettings(platform) hazard is avoided entirely. Per Q6 (an approved AC change) the Active/Inactive SelectFilter is removed; because that filter's default was what restricted the table to active kits, the base query must now scope to the active ids itself or the panel would silently start listing every kit under the heading 'Active Kit Users'. This node must land BEFORE the donut is deleted (t7) so the replacement always exists. Card counts are fixed (not filter-driven): they are point-in-time kit counts, not a date-ranged metric.
